title: AREG agent contract
description: Machine-readable form of the rules stated in docs/agent/. Prose remains authoritative; this file exists so a tool can check generated code mechanically instead of an agent re-reading a page. Keep in step with 20-service-interface.md section 3 and 31-consumer.md section 3.

legacy_names.description: areg was renamed throughout. Names an agent may recall from training data no longer exist. Never write an areg name from memory; grep for it.
legacy_names.removed_source: the rename commits themselves: git log -M --diff-filter=R --name-status -- 'framework/*', unioned with --diff-filter=D. tools/check_contract.py rule B-05 matches this exact list.
legacy_names.removed_scope: framework names only. An application is free to use any coding style and may legitimately define its own NE* name, so match these exactly rather than by prefix.
legacy_names.verified: each name in "removed" was checked against framework/ and defines nothing there. One survivor is deliberately absent from the list: namespace NEMultitargetRouterSettings in framework/mtrouter/app/MTRouterNames.hpp is current code, not a leftover.
legacy_names.detect: an identifier in "removed" above, or a camelCase call on an areg type

naming.description: How a name in a .siml document becomes a C++ name. <Name> is Overview/@Name.

rules.note: structures, enumerations and constants keep the document's spelling

consumer.note: The value is meaningful only when state == areg::DataState::DataIsOK. The first callback after subscribing may report it invalid.

service_connected.note: Called again on every reconnection. Subscribe here, not in the constructor.

Public.needs_router: only when provider and consumer are in different processes

logging.description: Logging is inert until a configuration file enables it. This is the most common cause of a correct LOG_* call producing no output.

config_file.note: A file placed beside the executable rather than in its config/ subdirectory is never read.

scope_name.note: Dot-joined, not underscore-joined. DEF_LOG_SCOPE(myapp_Worker, process_timer) is the scope myapp_Worker.process_timer.

scope_key.module: executable name without extension, or * for all applications
scope_key.pattern: scope name, with * as a trailing wildcard
scope_key.terminator_note: Optional. The parser strips a trailing ';' from any value, so its presence or absence changes nothing. The shipped areg.init writes one on every scope line.

remote_logging.purpose: collect the logs of several processes in one place
remote_logging.note: An application whose collector is absent runs normally and retries quietly, so silence is not evidence of a fault.

mtrouter.needed_when: provider and consumer are in different processes

logcollector.needed_when: you want the logs of several processes in one place
logcollector.persistence: Off by default. Start with --log=db to write a SQLite .sqlog into ./logs. Storing is the collector's job, not the observer's.

logobserver.needed_when: you want to watch collected logs live and change scope priorities at run time without restarting

prohibitions.rule: Never invent a member name on a generated base.
prohibitions.detect: member not derivable by the naming rules above

prohibitions.rule: REGISTER_DEPENDENCY must equal a provider role name exactly.
prohibitions.detect: dependency string with no matching BEGIN_REGISTER_COMPONENT role name

prohibitions.rule: Never call a request before the service is connected.
prohibitions.detect: request_* call outside service_connected or a later handler

prohibitions.rule: Never treat Disconnected, ConnectionLost or Failed as fatal.
prohibitions.detect: signal_quit or teardown on a non-terminal state
sleep, join, or an unbounded loop inside request_*, response_*, broadcast_*, on_*_update or process_timer

prohibitions.rule: Never include a header from a private/ folder.
Never register two components with the same role name in one process.
A watchdog timeout only bites while the watchdog manager runs, and it is off unless Application::setup() is called with startWatchdog true.
prohibitions.detect: a non-zero timeout in BEGIN_REGISTER_THREAD_EX or REGISTER_WORKER_THREAD_EX with no start_watchdog_manager and no setup(..., true, ...)

prohibitions.rule: The consumer name in REGISTER_WORKER_THREAD must equal the name the component answers to from worker_thread_consumer(); an unknown name yields nullptr and the worker thread runs nothing.
prohibitions.detect: a worker consumer string literal whose exact text appears nowhere else in the project

base_api_notes.rule: areg::String passed to a printf style log macro must use .as_string().
areg::ArrayList, areg::HashMap and areg::LinkedList expose no begin()/end(); a range-for does not compile. Iterate by index with size() and operator[].
Container element count is size(); emptiness is is_empty().
Container headers are ArrayList.hpp, HashMap.hpp and LinkedList.hpp, with no TE prefix.
Every framework method is snake_case and every public type is in namespace areg.
The IE prefix is gone from the public API; an interface is areg::ThreadConsumer, not IEThreadConsumer. Two IE names survive under component/private/, which no application may include.
Every framework method is snake_case: getName() is name(), getLength() is length(), isValid() is is_valid(), getTime() is to_time(), getAppName() is app_name().

checker_opt_out.applies_to: the line it sits on, or the line below it
